name: tour
title: Meet Oneirodex
blurb: A quick lap of the member app — Discover, the catalog, Systems, and the household.
transcript: Meet Oneirodex. A quick lap of the member app — Discover, the catalog, Systems, and the household.
Oneirodex is a self-hosted game library for a household. This is the member app, and Discover is where it opens.
Shelves surface what is new, what friends are playing, store deals, and curated rows an admin arranges.
Game Catalog is the whole library — every scanned title, with filters, badges and play buttons on each tile.
Systems groups the same library by console family, with a licensed catalog behind each console.
Chat, Friends and Notifications make it a household rather than a file share.
And everything you just saw is one Ctrl-K away from anywhere.
The rest of these clips take each of those areas one at a time.
That is meet oneirodex. The written guide is in the docs folder, at docs/user/getting-started.md.

name: library
title: Find a game in your library
blurb: Filters, segments, tile size and the actions on a tile.
transcript: Find a game in your library. Filters, segments, tile size and the actions on a tile.
Game Catalog lists every title Oneirodex has scanned and identified.
The segments across the top split games from soft titles, emulators and utilities.
Back to All.
Filters opens the full set — library, system, genre, theme, play path, and sort. Update, Missing, New and Lang are one-tap chips.
Type part of a name to narrow the grid as you go.
Clear it, and close the panel.
Every tile carries a Play button when browser play is available, a system chip, and a freshness badge — NEW here, UPDATE or MISSING after later scans.
The heart marks a favourite, and the menu holds download, collection and status actions.
Close the menu, then open a title to read its page.
That is find a game in your library. The written guide is in the docs folder, at docs/user/library-and-systems.md.

name: game-details
title: Read a game page
blurb: Download, play, install, versions, saved states and cheats — in one place.
transcript: Read a game page. Download, play, install, versions, saved states and cheats — in one place.
Open any tile and you land on the game page.
The header has the cover, size and status chips, and the actions: Download the files, Install through the desktop companion, or Play in browser where the system supports it.
Add to collection keeps household lists; Check updates and DLC asks the store side for newer versions.
Details on the right shows the library folder and playtime. Open path hands the folder to the desktop companion.
Versions lists the base game and every extra Oneirodex has matched.
Saved states and household cheat files live here too — browser play and the companion both read the same ones.
That is read a game page. The written guide is in the docs folder, at docs/user/library-and-systems.md.

name: discover
title: Discover — the storefront
blurb: Shelves, zones, pin and hide, and See all.
transcript: Discover — the storefront. Shelves, zones, pin and hide, and See all.
Discover is Oneirodex as a storefront for your own library.
Each row is a shelf. New Library Games, Most Downloaded, Curated for you — an admin orders them and can add custom ones with dates.
Pin keeps a shelf at the top for you; Hide removes it for your account only.
Arrows scroll a shelf, and See all opens it as a full page.
Everything here is your library, arranged — never a store queue.
That is discover — the storefront. The written guide is in the docs folder, at docs/user/library-and-systems.md.

name: systems
title: Systems and set completion
blurb: Console families, the licensed catalog, export packs and DAT completion.
transcript: Systems and set completion. Console families, the licensed catalog, export packs and DAT completion.
Systems is the same library grouped by console family.
Each console tile shows how many games you hold, whether they run in the browser, and a Catalog link to the licensed release list.
Export packs write a gamelist for ES-DE or Pegasus, so other front ends can show the same library without moving a file.
Completion compares your ROM sets against No-Intro and Redump DATs an admin uploads.
Region chips and percentages tell you exactly what is missing per system.
That is systems and set completion. The written guide is in the docs folder, at docs/user/library-and-systems.md.

name: play
title: Ways to play
blurb: Browser play, the desktop companion, and Big Picture for the TV.
transcript: Ways to play. Browser play, the desktop companion, and Big Picture for the TV.
Ways to Play lists every path to actually running a game.
Browser play uses WebRetro for supported consoles — cores are fetched at first boot, and cloud saves and cheats ride along.
The desktop companion installs, launches and updates PC titles; Catalog is browse-only.
On a tile, Play opens the game straight in a new tab.
Play buttons appear only where the system, the core and any BIOS are actually ready — no fake Play buttons.
Playtime keeps the record of what you ran and for how long.
That is ways to play. The written guide is in the docs folder, at docs/user/browser-play.md.

name: big-picture
title: Big Picture on the TV
blurb: A ten-foot interface driven by a controller or a few keys.
transcript: Big Picture on the TV. A ten-foot interface driven by a controller or a few keys.
Big Picture is the living-room view — large tiles, one focused title, controller-friendly.
Left and right browse.
Enter or A opens, D downloads, Y brings up friends, and B starts attract mode.
Escape blurs the focus and Home returns to the first tile.
That is big picture on the tv. The written guide is in the docs folder, at docs/user/browser-play.md.

name: chat-spaces
title: Chat, rooms and spaces
blurb: Household rooms, reactions and threads, voice, and invite-only spaces.
transcript: Chat, rooms and spaces. Household rooms, reactions and threads, voice, and invite-only spaces.
Chat slides out over whatever you are doing.
Expand gives it the whole pane.
Rooms are household channels — general, looking for players, whatever you add.
Messages take reactions, replies and threads.
Voice and Screenshare open a LiveKit session for the room when an admin has enabled it.
Switch to another room.
Spaces are servers of their own — text and voice channels, household-wide or invite-only. Paste an invite code to join one.
Pop out opens chat as its own window, handy on a second screen.
That is chat, rooms and spaces. The written guide is in the docs folder, at docs/user/social-and-voice.md.

name: friends
title: Friends and presence
blurb: The friends dock, adding people, and the pop-out companion.
transcript: Friends and presence. The friends dock, adding people, and the pop-out companion.
Friends is a dock, not a page — it opens from the rail and stays put.
It shows who in the household is online and what they are playing.
Add someone by username.
Pinned keeps the dock open across pages; Pop out makes it an always-on-top window with the desktop companion.
Chat and Activity jump straight to those surfaces.
That is friends and presence. The written guide is in the docs folder, at docs/user/social-and-voice.md.

name: collections
title: Collections, wishlist and favourites
blurb: The lists that organise a library — and Downloads for what you took.
transcript: Collections, wishlist and favourites. The lists that organise a library — and Downloads for what you took.
Collections are named lists you build from any game page or tile menu.
Wishlist tracks titles you want — the release calendar and store deals feed it.
Favourites is the heart on a tile, collected.
Downloads lists what you have taken from the library and the zips still being built.
Updates is the inbox for new versions and extras that scans find for titles you hold.
That is collections, wishlist and favourites. The written guide is in the docs folder, at docs/user/library-and-systems.md.

name: calendar-news
title: Calendar, news and activity
blurb: What is coming, what happened, and what the household did.
transcript: Calendar, news and activity. What is coming, what happened, and what the household did.
Release calendar is IGDB's schedule, filtered to what you own or wish for. List or Month view.
Month lays the same releases on a grid.
News collects store and publisher feeds an admin has turned on.
Activity is the household timeline — scans, downloads, plays and posts.
Notifications are yours alone: mentions, invites, finished scans.
That is calendar, news and activity. The written guide is in the docs folder, at docs/user/library-and-systems.md.

name: preferences
title: Themes, rooms, icons and fonts
blurb: Make it yours from the Preferences modal.
transcript: Themes, rooms, icons and fonts. Make it yours from the Preferences modal.
Preferences lives under the account menu.
Library sets your page size and default sort.
Decade rooms are the scenery — a 1980s wood den, a 90s bedroom, an arcade floor. Browser play uses the same room.
Colour cabinets are palettes that still sit in a room rather than a flat colour.
Icon packs are independent of the theme — Outline, Filled, Duotone, Pixel, Soft and Mono.
Fonts offer era faces per system; tile size is a continuous slider.
Save, and the whole app takes the new look.
That is themes, rooms, icons and fonts. The written guide is in the docs folder, at docs/user/preferences-themes.md.

name: command-palette
title: The command palette
blurb: Ctrl-K or Cmd-K to search titles and jump anywhere.
transcript: The command palette. Ctrl-K or Cmd-K to search titles and jump anywhere.
From any page, press Control K.
Empty, it lists everywhere you can go — and, once you have played something, your recent titles and household favourites.
Type two letters to search titles and destinations.
Enter goes there.
That is the command palette. The written guide is in the docs folder, at docs/user/getting-started.md.

name: help-support
title: Help and reporting a problem
blurb: The in-app guide, and Report issue straight to the admin inbox.
transcript: Help and reporting a problem. The in-app guide, and Report issue straight to the admin inbox.
Help is the in-app guide — pick a topic and the answer opens underneath.
Expand all reads it straight through.
Topics cover browser play, controllers, cheats, translations and the licence.
Report sends an issue to the admin's Support inbox, and on to GitHub when configured.
That is help and reporting a problem. The written guide is in the docs folder, at docs/user/faq.md.

name: admin-libraries
title: Libraries and scans
blurb: Add a library, point a scan at a folder, watch the job.
transcript: Libraries and scans. Add a library, point a scan at a folder, watch the job.
Libraries and scans is where a library begins.
Each library is a platform plus a folder. Select rows to scan, edit, group or delete them.
Scan chooses a library and a folder — on this box, a NAS share, or any declared scan location — and whether games are folders or files.
Options cover missing games, missing images, extras, and HowLongToBeat.
Scan jobs shows every run with progress, and Unmatched holds what could not be identified for you to fix by hand.
That is libraries and scans. The written guide is in the docs folder, at docs/admin/libraries-and-scans.md.

name: admin-discover
title: Shelves and events
blurb: Arrange Discover: reorder, hide, and add custom shelves with dates.
transcript: Shelves and events. Arrange Discover: reorder, hide, and add custom shelves with dates.
Discovery sections controls what members see on Discover.
Drag to reorder. Toggle Visible to hide a built-in shelf without deleting it.
Add shelf creates a custom one — a hand-picked list, or a library, platform or genre filter.
Give it a start and end date and it becomes an event: a seasonal row that appears and retires on its own.
Newsletter, Announcements and Attract mode sit alongside it under Content.
That is shelves and events. The written guide is in the docs folder, at docs/admin/discover-sections.md.

name: admin-ops
title: Ops health
blurb: Is everything healthy — services, queues, companions, the log.
transcript: Ops health. Is everything healthy — services, queues, companions, the log.
The admin Dashboard is the at-a-glance board: libraries, games, health, scans, disk.
Ops goes deeper — CPU, memory, database, watch folders, and every service with its status.
Tiles resize and the layout is yours; Reset layout puts it back.
Services shows LiveKit, the malware scanner, companions and queues.
The recent log is filterable by level, type and text, and Full log opens the whole thing.
The same numbers are on slash pulse and slash awake for your monitoring.
That is ops health. The written guide is in the docs folder, at docs/admin/ops-summary.md.

name: admin-users
title: Users, invites and support
blurb: Household membership, invite links, roles and the support inbox.
transcript: Users, invites and support. Household membership, invite links, roles and the support inbox.
Users lists every member with their role — admin, librarian, member or child.
Invites are how people join: generate a link, set its quota, hand it over.
Whitelist pre-approves addresses when registration is open.
Support inbox receives what members send from Report, and can mirror to GitHub Issues.
That is users, invites and support. The written guide is in the docs folder, at docs/admin/support-inbox.md.

name: admin-settings
title: Settings, features and integrations
blurb: Server settings, module toggles, metadata providers, SSO.
transcript: Settings, features and integrations. Server settings, module toggles, metadata providers, SSO.
Settings is the index — library and matching, play and emulation, presentation, extend.
Features toggles whole modules: arr, AI assist, VR browse, free games, remote play.
Integrations holds the keys — IGDB, SteamGridDB, RetroAchievements, email, and OIDC single sign-on, which stays off until you turn it on.
Themes uploads packs and resets shipped defaults after a deploy; picking a look is per member.
Emulator profiles map cores and BIOS per system, and say honestly what can run.
That is settings, features and integrations. The written guide is in the docs folder, at docs/admin/settings-modules.md.

name: admin-art
title: Art studio and extensions
blurb: Covers without a cloud, the image queue, and reference sets.
transcript: Art studio and extensions. Covers without a cloud, the image queue, and reference sets.
Art studio paints a cover from a title — motifs, bezels, initials — with a local renderer. No cloud AI.
Type a name and the preview updates.
Generate writes the full pack; Pick and queue fetches SteamGridDB or IGDB art instead.
Backup and stock keeps fallbacks, and System marks holds a badge per console.
Extensions lists library extensions — DLC, patches, translations — and Reference sets take your DAT uploads.
That is art studio and extensions. The written guide is in the docs folder, at docs/admin/theme-fonts-and-images.md.
